breakfast.name: Salteñas (Baked Empanadas)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, sugar, annatto-infused oil, egg, water
Filling: 300g beef (diced small), 2 potatoes (diced), 1 cup peas, 1 onion, hardboiled egg, olives, cumin, aji pepper, gelatin broth
instructions: Make dough with annatto oil for golden color, chill
Cook filling: sauté beef, onions, add potatoes, peas, spices
Add gelatin broth so filling sets when cold
Chill filling until firm
Fill dough circles, crimp edges into decorative ridge
Bake at 220°C 25 min until golden
breakfast.description: Bolivia's beloved morning pastry — juicy, spiced meat in golden dough.

breakfast.name: Api con Pastel (Purple Corn Drink with Pastry)
instructions: Boil purple corn in water with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel 30 min
Strain, sweeten to taste
Make pastry dough, fill with cheese
Fry pastries until golden
Serve hot api alongside cheese pastels
breakfast.description: Hot purple corn drink paired with fried cheese pastries.

breakfast.name: Api con Pastel (Purple Corn Drink with Pastry)
ingredients: Api: 2 cups purple corn flour, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel, sugar, water
Pastel: flour, cheese filling, oil for frying
instructions: For api: simmer purple corn flour with water, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel
Stir until thick and fragrant
Sweeten with sugar
For pastel: make simple dough, fill with cheese
Fry pastels until golden
Serve hot api alongside warm pastels
breakfast.description: Hot purple corn drink with fried cheese pastries — the classic Bolivian street breakfast, especially in La Paz's cold mornings.

lunch.name: Pique Macho
instructions: Fry potato cubes until golden
Sear beef cubes in hot oil
Fry hot dog slices
Layer on platter: fries, beef, hot dogs
Top with tomato, onion, locoto peppers, egg slices
Season with cumin and salt
lunch.description: A towering platter of beef, sausage, fries, and peppers.

lunch.name: Sopa de Maní (Peanut Soup)
instructions: Brown beef ribs, cover with water, simmer 30 min
Blend peanuts to smooth paste
Add peanut paste to broth
Add potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, spices
Simmer until vegetables tender
Serve topped with crispy fried pasta noodles
lunch.description: Creamy peanut soup with beef — a Cochabamba specialty.

lunch.name: Sopa de Maní (Peanut Soup)
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onion and tomato, add cumin
Add water, return meat, simmer 20 min
Add potatoes, cook 10 min
Add ground peanuts dissolved in broth — stir to prevent lumps
Add pasta, cook 8 min
Garnish with parsley and fried potato strips
lunch.description: Creamy peanut soup — Bolivia's most beloved soup, rich and deeply nutty. Served across the country for almuerzo (lunch).

dinner.name: Silpancho
instructions: Pound beef very thin, bread and fry
Fry potato slices
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Layer on plate: rice, fried potatoes, breaded beef, fried egg
Top with fresh salsa of tomato, onion, locoto, parsley
dinner.description: A layered plate of rice, potatoes, breaded beef, and a fried egg.

dinner.name: Fricasé (Spicy Pork Stew)
instructions: Brown pork pieces
Blend onions, garlic, aji paste
Add to pork with cumin, oregano, water
Simmer with hominy 60 min
Add chuño, cook 30 more min
Serve with bread
dinner.description: A hearty, spicy pork and hominy stew.

dinner.name: Pique a lo Macho
instructions: Fry potatoes into thick chips, set aside
Sear beef slices quickly over high heat
Add hot dogs, onion, tomato, locotos
Toss together with cumin and salt
Pile on top of fried potatoes
Garnish with hard-boiled egg quarters
Serve on a big shared plate
dinner.description: A macho pile of seared beef, hot dogs, peppers, and fried potatoes — Cochabamba's famous feast dish, always shared.

snacks.name: Anticuchos (Beef Heart Skewers)
instructions: Trim and cube beef heart
Marinate in aji panca, cumin, garlic, vinegar 2+ hours
Thread onto skewers
Grill over high heat, basting with marinade
Serve with boiled potatoes and aji sauce
snacks.description: Char-grilled beef heart skewers — Andean street food.

snacks.name: Tucumanas (Fried Empanadas)
ingredients: Filling: chicken or beef, potato, peas, hard-boiled egg, olive, cumin, ají
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Prepare filling: cook seasoned meat with potato, peas, cumin
Roll dough circles, fill with meat mixture, egg slice, olive
Fold into half-moon, seal edges tightly
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with llajwa (tomato-locoto salsa)
snacks.description: Bolivian fried empanadas from Sucre — crunchier and richer than their baked cousins, always with llajwa.

snacks.name: Salteñas (Bolivian Empanadas)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, sugar, ají amarillo powder (for color), butter, egg, warm water
Filling: beef or chicken (diced small), potatoes (diced), peas, hard-boiled egg (chopped)
Jigote sauce: ají amarillo paste, onion, cumin, gelatin, beef broth
instructions: Make jigote: cook onion, ají paste, cumin, add broth and gelatin, fold in meat and vegetables
Refrigerate filling until set — the gelatin is essential, it melts into juicy broth when baked
Make dough with flour, sugar, ají powder, butter, egg — it must be slightly sweet
Roll out, cut circles, fill generously
Crimp the seal into a rope pattern along the top — this must hold or juice leaks
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 min until golden with a sweet, slightly charred crust
Eat immediately — bite corner, sip the broth, then eat
The broth-inside-pastry concept is what makes these viral — South America's soup dumpling
snacks.description: Bolivia's morning obsession — a sweet-dough empanada with a juicy, soupy filling held together by gelatin that melts when baked. You eat it by biting a corner and sipping the broth first. Called 'South America's soup dumpling,' salteña-eating technique videos are viral content gold.

desserts.name: Tawa-Tawas (Fried Dough Spirals)
instructions: Mix dough with flour, eggs, butter, sugar, zest, anise
Rest 20 min
Roll thin, cut into strips
Shape into spirals
Deep fry until golden
Drizzle with honey or cane syrup
desserts.description: Crispy fried dough spirals drizzled with honey.

desserts.name: Tawa-Tawas (Fried Dough Spirals)
instructions: Mix flour, egg, sugar, anise, cinnamon, orange zest
Knead into smooth dough
Roll into long ropes, coil into spiral shapes
Deep fry until golden
Drizzle with honey or cane syrup
desserts.description: Spiral-shaped fried dough scented with anise and cinnamon — sold at Bolivian festivals and street corners.

drinks.name: Api Morado (Purple Corn Drink)
instructions: Boil purple corn with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel
Simmer 30 min until thick and purple
Strain
Sweeten to taste
Serve hot, sprinkle with ground cinnamon
drinks.description: Hot, thick purple corn drink — a La Paz morning ritual.

drinks.name: Chicha (Fermented Corn Beer)
instructions: Soak and sprout corn 3 days
Grind sprouted corn
Boil in water to make sweet wort
Cool, let ferment naturally 3-7 days
Strain
Serve in clay cups

drinks.name: Mocochinchi (Dried Peach Drink)
instructions: Boil dried peaches with cinnamon and cloves
Simmer 15 min until peaches are plump
Sweeten with sugar
Cool and refrigerate
Serve cold with a rehydrated peach in each glass
drinks.description: Cinnamon-spiced dried peach drink — Bolivia's refreshing street beverage, sold from carts in every city plaza.
